headline: India Slashes Cancer Drug Prices by Up to 70% for 137 Medicines
meta_description: India's Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers expands price controls on 137 cancer medicines, cutting costs by up to 70% starting November 9.
summary_short: India is making cancer treatment more affordable by cutting prices on 137 medicines by up to 70%, including immunotherapy drugs for over 20 cancer types.
body:
India's Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers announced Saturday that it will reduce prices on as many as 137 cancer drugs by up to 70 percent, effective November 9, in a sweeping effort to make lifesaving treatment accessible to more people across the country.

The price controls limit trade margins on these medicines to 30 percent of the maximum retail price. The affected drugs include immunotherapy treatments used for over 20 types of cancer, alongside medicines for breast, prostate, and colon cancers, among others.

This expansion of price regulations reflects India's ongoing commitment to balancing pharmaceutical innovation with patient affordability—a critical challenge in a country where cancer treatment costs can push families into financial hardship.

Trade margins limited to 30% of maximum retail price
Covers immunotherapy drugs for 20+ cancer types
India's Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers issued directive
